channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar advances as US labor market weakness pressures the USD
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5890 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.36% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Gradual improvement with tariff risks – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada’s (RBC) Nathan Janzen reports that Canada’s labour market strengthened in July, with a 75k employment gain following robust increases in May and June and a decline in the unemployment rate to 6.4%.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs near two-month highs as NFP turns negative
item.description: The AUD/USD pair surged to its highest in nearly two months past 0.7070 earlier on Friday, following the release of the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. The move owes nothing to Australia.

item.title: NY Fed inflation expectations ease modestly in the short term
item.description: The New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations shows that households’ inflation expectations decreased slightly over the short-term horizon and remained unchanged at the medium and longer-term horizons. One-year inflation expectations eased from 3.7% in June to 3.6% in July

item.title: Natural Gas: Higher price forecasts on LNG squeeze – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank has revised Gas and German power price forecasts higher, citing tighter European storage, increased reliance on LNG and structural constraints on Qatari exports. The phase-out of Russian Gas from 2027 adds upside risk.

item.title: US Dollar: Payrolls-driven consolidation as CPI looms – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that the US Dollar (USD) weakened after the disappointing July Payrolls report, but see limited downside against G10 currencies unless softer US inflation further reduces Fed hike expectations.

item.title: Gold heads for best week since January after disappointing NFP
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its recovery on Friday as weaker-than-expected US payroll growth weighs on the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,356 after hitting $4,371, its highest level since June 17.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Fed focus shifts to jobs – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO’s Chief Economist Nick Kounis highlights renewed US labour market weakness, with Nonfarm Payrolls falling and household employment data softening. He notes the unemployment rate declined as labour force participation dropped to multi-decade lows, signalling cyclical weakness.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains against US Dollar after surprise decline in US payrolls
item.description: USD/CHF edges lower on Friday, erasing most of the previous day’s gains as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following a downside surprise in the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.8080, down 0.53% on the day.

item.title: Canada: Labour market resilience supports cautious Bank of Canada – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) economists Matthieu Arseneau and Alexandra Ducharme highlight robust Canadian labour data for July, with 75.1K jobs added, a lower unemployment rate and stronger private-sector hiring.

item.title: Gold: Discretionary demand keeps bulls in control - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight that strong discretionary and Asian buying is supporting Gold, even as CTA (Commodity Trading Advisors) positioning has plateaued.

item.title: Canadian Dollar jumps after North American jobs double surprise
item.description: USD/CAD declines sharply on Friday, trading around 1.3940 at the time of writing, down 0.53% on the day, hitting its lowest level since June.

item.title: United States Dollar Index tumbles as NFP shock trims Fed hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the buck’s value against a basket of six currencies, is down 0.36% to 99.58 following a weaker-than-expected US jobs report. The DXY hit 99.41 after the jobs report release, its lowest level since June 15.

item.title: Brent: Volatile path as Hormuz risk lingers – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch sees continued volatility in Brent as Strait of Hormuz negotiations remain unresolved and inventories tighten.

item.title: US Dollar: Weak payrolls cloud Fed path – ING
item.description: ING’s Chief International Economist James Knightley notes that the weak July US jobs report has pushed market pricing away from a September Federal Reserve rate hike, with the Dollar softening and 2-year yields falling.

item.title: Fed's Barkin: Jobs data is more low hire, low fire
item.description: Thomas Barkin, President of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Richmond, participated in an online event hosted by the National Association for Business Economics on Friday.

item.title: Copper: Tariff-driven tightness faces policy risk – ING
item.description: ING Commodities Strategist Ewa Manthey highlights that Copper has surged back near record highs as traders accelerate shipments into the US ahead of potential import tariffs, tightening physical markets and draining LME inventories.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Labour strength and BoC stance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence highlight a strong Canadian labour market, with July employment up 75k and unemployment at 6.4%.

item.title: Mexico: Banxico extended hold stance – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish reports that Banxico left its policy rate at 6.50%, signalling an extended pause as inflation hovers near target and real rates sit close to neutral.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Weak US payrolls fuel breakout above 50-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) jumps nearly 4% on Friday as buying accelerates following a decisive break above the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) near $62. At the time of writing, the grey metal trades around $63.94 after briefly testing the $65 psychological mark.

item.title: Silver: Solar demand headwinds emerge – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes that the Silver price has surged over 10% this week to USD 63.9 per troy ounce, its highest level since late June, pulling the gold/silver ratio back below 70.

item.title: Japanese Yen surges as weak US jobs data questions Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: USD/JPY falls toward 157.40 on Friday, down 0.65% on the day at the time of writing, as the US Dollar (USD) comes under heavy selling pressure following a much weaker-than-expected US employment report.

item.title: British Pound climbs above 1.3500 after weak US NFP data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after a disappointing US Nonfarm Payrolls report prompts traders to scale back bets on Federal Reserve (Fed) interest-rate hikes. At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades around 1.3506, hovering near three-week highs.

item.title: Euro surges as shocking US NFP reverses Fed September hike expectations
item.description: EUR/USD jumps 0.43% on the day and trades around 1.1570 at the time of writing, as the US Dollar (USD) comes under heavy selling pressure following a much weaker-than-expected US employment report.

item.title: Equities: AI profitability doubts grow – Nordea
item.description: Nordea analysts Kirsti Sunde Midttun and Ole Håkon Eek-Nielsen argue that AI profitability faces structural pressure from high inference costs, rapid model depreciation and growing competition from free and open alternatives.

item.title: Breaking: US Nonfarm Payrolls fall by 23K in July vs. +80K expected
item.description: Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) in the United States (US) declined by 23K in July, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Friday. This print followed the 20K increase (revised from 57K) recorded in June and fell short of the market expectation for an increase of 80K by a wide margin.

item.title: Canada's Unemployment Rate drops to 6.4% in July
item.description: Statistics Canada reported on Friday that the Unemployment Rate decreased to 6.4% in July, below what markets were expecting.

item.title: India: Inflation steady, trade deficit persists – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Econs team expects India’s July inflation to remain steady at 4.4% year-on-year, with core readings staying below 4% thanks to softer precious metals. Food staples show mixed trends, while fuel price adjustments may lift utilities and fuel components.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention skepticism meets BoJ repricing – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights growing market skepticism about Japan’s FX interventions, despite sizeable recent operations that triggered sharp but temporary Japanese Yen (JPY) rallies.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Mixed momentum signals point to more consolidation
item.description: The Euro (EUR) edges higher against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, although price action has been confined to a narrow range over the past ten trading days, suggesting that the mid-July rebound from below 0.8500 is losing steam beneath a dense cluster of moving averages.
